name: Five Up Dominoes
description: Domino game in the Fives family. All doubles are spinners. Score when layout pip total is a multiple of 5. Play to 61 points.
origin: United States (California and Southwestern US; popularized by Dominic C. Armanino)

history.origins: Five Up is a domino game in the Fives family. Dominic C. Armanino made it extremely popular in California and the Southwestern United States with books and tournaments.
timeline: 20th century: Popularized in California and Southwestern US by Dominic C. Armanino with books and tournaments.

setup.dealing: Each player receives five tiles. The remaining tiles form the boneyard (stock).
setup.equipment: Double-six domino set; cribbage board recommended for scoring.

rules.objective: Be the first player or partnership to reach 61 points. Score during play by making the open ends of the layout total a multiple of five; at end of each hand, subtract penalty points for pips left in hand (rounded to nearest multiple of five, divided by five).
rules.gameplay: Domino game in the Fives family. All doubles are spinners. Score when layout pip total is a multiple of 5. Play to 61 points.
keyRules: Five tiles each; rest is boneyard. Lead plays any tile; others match open ends. All doubles are spinners (crosswise). If you cannot play, draw from boneyard until you can play or it is empty; if you draw a playable tile, play it immediately and turn ends. Hand ends when one player dominoes or all are blocked. After each play, if open-end total is a multiple of 5, score that total divided by 5. At hand end, pips in hand rounded to nearest 5, divided by 5, subtracted from your score. First to 61 wins.

strategy.basic: Count outstanding tiles; aim to make layout totals that are multiples of 5. When leading, play a ten-point tile (5-5 or 4-6) if possible.
strategy.intermediate: Balance scoring, blocking, and playing to domino. Leave small totals for the next player to limit their scoring. Use information when an opponent draws (they lacked that pip).
strategy.advanced: Pursue scoring early when distribution is unknown; switch to blocking when you can count suits and force a blocked game with you holding fewest pips. Dominoing gives lead next hand.
tips: Doubles give control of layout arms; play them to limit opponent options.
Rounding: 1-2 rounds to 5 (1 pt penalty), 1-1 rounds to 0.

variations.name: Armanino scoring
variations.description: Winner scores opponents' total pips (rounded to nearest 5, divided by 5) at hand end. Blocked two-hand: winner scores opponents' total pips. Three-hand blocked: only lowest pip holder scores the difference. Turn to lead may rotate clockwise.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Armanino scoring changes end-of-hand scoring rules; engine overrides for this variant not yet mapped.

scoring.description: After each tile is set, sum the pips on all open ends of the layout; if the total is a multiple of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20...), the player scores that total divided by 5. An exposed double counts both its pips until tiles have been played on both sides of it. At end of hand, each player's remaining pips are rounded to the nearest multiple of 5, divided by 5, and subtracted from their score. First to 61 points wins.
scoring.winCondition: First player or partnership to reach 61 points wins. Tie: play further hands until one leads.
